Name: Department of parks and recreation’s response to complaints of risk of imminent harm posed by trees on public property.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the department of parks and recreation’s response to complaints of risk of imminent harm posed by trees on public property

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Parks and Recreation

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Parks and Recreation (Parks) to inspect a publicly-owned tree upon receipt of a tree inspection request or referral that states that the tree poses an imminent risk of harm to persons or property. Parks would have 72 hours to inspect the tree. Within 72 hours of that inspection, Parks must report back to the person that made the request or referral on what actions the department will take to mitigate the risk and a timeline for these actions. If Parks does not believe the tree presents a risk, Parks must provide a written explanation to the person as to why the tree is not a risk. Finally, Parks would be required to provide disaggregated information, as part of its annual tree reporting to the Mayor and the Speaker of the Council, on tree inspection requests or referrals that state that the tree poses an imminent risk of harm to persons or property.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to the department of parks and recreation’s response to complaints of risk of imminent harm posed by trees on public property

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Section 18-157 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 20 for the year 2022, is amended to read as follows:
§ 18-157 Tree inspections and health assessments. a. The department shall inspect each tree under its jurisdiction over 6 inches in caliper, to determine if any issue threatens the health of such tree or causes such tree to pose a threat to public safety, at least once between each time such tree is pruned by the department or by a person authorized by the department to perform routine scheduled maintenance of such tree. Such inspection shall not be required for trees in forests and natural areas, and shall be limited to inspections of trees located on streets and trees located in landscaped parks, which for purposes of this section are referred to as “covered trees[”].”
b. The department shall post on its website a description of the process used and the factors considered by the department, and by any person authorized by the department, to determine when inspections are performed on trees under the jurisdiction of the department in order to assess the health of such trees.
c. 1. In addition to the inspection requirements set forth in subdivision a of this section, whenever the department receives any request or referral for inspection of a covered tree through the 311 customer service center or other means that states an imminent risk of harm to persons or property posed by such tree, the department shall, within 72 hours of receipt of such request or referral, inspect such tree.
2. Within 72 hours of such inspection, the department shall provide a written report to the person that submitted such request or referral, which states:
(a) If the department agrees that such tree poses an imminent risk of harm to persons or property, the department’s next steps in mitigating such risk and the timeline for such steps; or
(b) If the department does not agree that such tree poses an imminent risk of harm to persons or property, an explanation of such disagreement.
d. No later than November 1 of each year, the department shall, for the period covering the immediately preceding fiscal year, submit an annual report to the mayor and the speaker of the council that includes, but is not limited to, the following information, with disaggregated reporting pertaining to requests or referrals for inspection of a covered tree through the 311 customer service center or other means that state an imminent risk of harm to persons or property posed by a covered tree:
1. The total number and location of all covered trees inspected by the department or persons authorized by the department, the result of such inspections and the actions taken by the department in response to such inspections;
2. The number and location of requests or referrals for inspection of a covered tree through the 311 [citizen] customer service center or other means and the number of such trees that were inspected by the department or a person authorized by the department;
3. The date of each referral or request for an inspection of a covered tree and the reason, if any, that was provided for such referral or request;
4. The action taken by the department in response to each request or referral for inspection of a covered tree and the date such action was taken; and
5. A regularly updated map on the website of the department that displays each covered tree that has been inspected, the result of such inspection and the action taken by the department in response to the result of such inspection.
§ 2. Section 23-312 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as added by local law number 61 for the year 2025, is amended to read as follows:
§ 23-312 Tree pruning complaints or requests for service. The 311 customer service center, in consultation with the department of parks and recreation, shall provide to any person who submits a complaint or request for service relating to the pruning of any tree under the jurisdiction of the department of parks and recreation:
1. A link to the map required by paragraph 5 of subdivision [c] d of section 18-157;
2. A link to a page of the website of the department of parks and recreation that includes information about tree pruning and a map showing completed and scheduled tree pruning activities by such department; [and]
3. Information or resources about a program to train and certify volunteers in the pruning of trees; and
4. A summary of the inspection and reporting requirements imposed upon the department under subdivision c of section 18-157.
§ 3. This local law takes effect 120 days after becoming law.
